title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
summary: Given an array of strings, find the highest product of the lengths of two distinct strings that share no common letters, or return 0 if no such pair exists.
statement: Given an array of strings, find the highest product of the lengths of two distinct strings that share no common letters, or return 0 if no such pair exists.
constraints: 2–1000 words, each with 1–1000 lowercase English letters.
Choose two different positions whose words share NO letter. Maximize the product of their full lengths, counting repeated letters in each length. Return 0 if no pair works.
target_time_complexity: O(L+u^2), L = total characters, u = distinct masks
hints: Only letter membership determines whether a pair is compatible.
Encode the 26 lowercase letters as bits; two masks are disjoint when their bitwise AND is zero.
Store the greatest full word length for each mask, then compare every pair of masks with AND=0.
Keeping only the longest word for a mask is safe because all words with that mask have the same compatible partners.
editorial: A 26-bit mask records membership, while length is kept separately. Any two words with a common letter have a nonzero mask intersection. Compress equal masks to their longest length and maximize products of compatible pairs. The oracle compares explicit character sets for every original pair.

tests.explanation: abcw and xtfn share no letters and have lengths 4 and 4, giving 16.
aa and bbb are disjoint and give 2×3=6. Repeated letters count toward length.
